summary.text: Brendan Boyle is the Democratic incumbent for Pennsylvania's 2nd District, a Philadelphia native who served in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives from 2009 to 2015 before his election to Congress in 2014. He is the ranking member of the House Budget Committee and also serves on the Ways and Means Committee. According to his official biography, he is a visiting lecturer at Princeton University and lead Democrat on the U.S. delegation to the NATO Parliamentary Assembly.

paragraphs.text: Boyle was born in Philadelphia in 1977, and his official biography says he was born and raised in the city, the son of an immigrant, with a father who worked as a SEPTA janitor and a mother who was a school crossing guard.

He was the first in his family to attend college and earned a bachelor's degree in government from the University of Notre Dame in 1999 and a Master of Public Policy from Harvard University's John F. Kennedy School of Government in 2005.
Before entering office he worked for American Management Systems as a consultant, as a radio broadcaster and as an adjunct professor.

Boyle was elected to the Pennsylvania House of Representatives in 2008 and served from 2009 to 2015; according to his official biography, he was the first Democrat to represent his legislative district.
His brother, Kevin Boyle, was elected to the state House in 2010, which his official biography describes as making them the first brothers to serve together in that chamber.
Boyle was elected to the U.S. House in 2014, a win his official biography describes as an upset over three better-funded rivals, and it says he is now in his sixth term.
In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), he is ranking member of the House Budget Committee and serves on the Ways and Means Committee's Health and Trade subcommittees.

According to his official pages, he also serves as lead Democrat for the U.S. congressional delegation to the NATO Parliamentary Assembly, is a visiting lecturer at Princeton University, and co-chairs several caucuses including the Auto Care, Blue Collar and EU caucuses.
